buyer_roles.title: Hypothesis: VP/Head of Battery R&D at a cell or EV maker
buyer_roles.why: Hypothesis: Work on phospho-olivine electrodes, lithium-metal anodes and dendrite suppression targets teams that choose electrode materials and cell chemistries to raise energy density and safety.

buyer_roles.title: Hypothesis: Director of Solid-State Battery Development
buyer_roles.why: Hypothesis: Findings on lithium penetration through inorganic solid electrolytes, tied to defect size and critical current density, are relevant to leaders deciding electrolyte materials, processing and failure-mode tests for solid-state cells.

buyer_roles.title: Hypothesis: Head of Decarbonization or Energy Storage Strategy at an industrial or utility firm
buyer_roles.why: Hypothesis: The net-zero energy systems review points to planners who must integrate storage and reliable electricity supply into decarbonization pathways.

industries.name: Hypothesis: Lithium-ion and lithium-metal battery manufacturing
industries.why: Hypothesis: Electrode materials and lithium-metal anode stability work map directly to cell producers seeking higher capacity and safer cycling.

industries.name: Hypothesis: Solid-state battery and solid electrolyte developers
industries.why: Hypothesis: Analysis of lithium infiltration through sulfide and garnet electrolytes addresses a core failure mode for this segment.

industries.name: Hypothesis: Grid-scale and long-duration energy storage
industries.why: Hypothesis: The decarbonization review stresses reliable electricity supply, which suggests demand for storage technologies, though no buyer demand is verified here.

needs.text: Hypothesis: Battery developers need ways to suppress lithium dendrites and electrolyte decomposition in lithium-metal cells. Reasoning: the polysulfide and nitrate additive work describes these as safety and Coulombic efficiency problems.

Hypothesis: Solid-state cell makers need to understand and prevent short circuits caused by lithium infiltration at electrolyte defects. Reasoning: infiltration is reported to start above a critical current density near surface flaws, so defect control and characterization may matter.

Hypothesis: Electrode makers need conductive, scalable cathode and nanostructured electrode materials. Reasoning: the phospho-olivine and virus-templated nanowire work address electronic conductivity and room-temperature synthesis and assembly for thin, flexible batteries.

expansion_segments.name: Hypothesis: Flexible and thin-film battery makers
expansion_segments.why: Hypothesis: Virus-templated nanowire assembly is framed around smaller, more flexible batteries, which may suit compact or wearable power devices.

expansion_segments.name: Hypothesis: Hard-to-decarbonize sectors such as aviation, long-distance transport and heavy industry
expansion_segments.why: Hypothesis: The review names these sectors as difficult to decarbonize, so higher-energy-density or safer storage could be relevant to them.

expansion_segments.name: Hypothesis: Battery testing, failure analysis and materials characterization services
expansion_segments.why: Hypothesis: Mechanistic studies of dendrite and crack-driven lithium penetration suggest a need for diagnostics and defect analysis tools.
